title: Minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee March 17-18, 2026
summary: FOMC minutes from the March 17-18, 2026 meeting reveal a significant repricing of monetary policy expectations driven by Middle East conflict-induced energy price spikes and AI disruption concerns. Near-term rate cut expectations shifted materially higher, with markets not fully pricing a cut until December and approximately 30% probability of rate hikes through early 2027. The committee noted elevated inflation pressures while acknowledging solid GDP growth and stable unemployment.
key_points: Front-month crude oil futures increased approximately 50% during the intermeeting period due to Middle East conflict, with longer-dated futures rising significantly less, suggesting markets viewed the price spike as relatively transitory
Options-implied probability of rate hikes through early 2027 increased to about 30%, with no rate cuts fully priced in until December
Desk survey median still showed two 25bp rate cuts for 2026, though respondents pushed out timing slightly and some shifted expectations post-survey
Broad equity prices fell approximately 5% over the period; software sector underperformed sharply due to AI-related concerns affecting leveraged loan prices
Notable increases in redemption requests at several private credit funds offering limited liquidity through quarterly redemption opportunities
Standing repo operations reached $30 billion on one day (third-largest volume since inception), suggesting greater willingness to use operations following December changes
Reserves projected to average approximately $3 trillion through September after trough in late April; monthly pace of RMPs likely to be reduced significantly after April
why_it_matters: The significant upward repricing of Fed rate expectations in just six weeks highlights how quickly market consensus can shift on macro catalysts. The divergence between futures/options markets (pricing no cuts) and the Desk survey median (two cuts) signals deep uncertainty about the policy path. Private credit fund redemption pressures and software sector weakness suggest potential stress points in market structure worth monitoring.
macro_context: Middle East conflict drove a 50% spike in front-month crude oil futures, raising near-term inflation expectations (one-year inflation swap rate rose ~50bp). Elevated energy prices are now expected to cause other central banks (ECB, BoC, SNB) to hike modestly rather than ease as previously expected. However, longer-dated inflation compensation was little changed, suggesting markets view the supply shock as temporary.
market_structure_context: Treasury market liquidity diminished somewhat in line with yield volatility but continued to function well. Standing repo usage reached $30 billion on a high-settlement day, with interdealer repo rates not much above the standing repo rate, indicating improved operational uptake following December framework changes. Private credit fund redemption requests increased notably, warranting continued staff monitoring.

~$30 billion — standing repo usage on peak settlement day
~$3 trillion — projected average reserves through September
~5% — broad equity price decline over period
~30% — probability of rate hikes through early 2027 per options prices
~50bp — one-year inflation swap rate increase over period
